name: Fourth-wave feminism
summary: Fourth-wave feminism is the feminism of roughly the 2010s onward, organised largely through social media. It campaigns against sexual harassment and violence, rape culture, everyday sexism, body shaming and pay inequality, and treats intersectionality as its guiding framework. It is generally inclusive of LGBTQ+ people and invites men to take part as allies.
scope: The mainstream English-language, online-driven movement as documented in Wikipedia's fourth-wave article and its flagship campaigns: #MeToo (Tarana Burke, Alyssa Milano), the Everyday Sexism Project (Laura Bates) and HeForShe (Emma Watson), with Kimberle Crenshaw's intersectionality as theoretical base. It excludes the trans-exclusionary faction noted in Latin America, and earlier waves. Economic and constitutional questions are mostly outside its agenda, so many answers are low-confidence inferences.

sources.usedFor: Aims of documenting everyday sexism and policy work.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Not a defining issue, but a movement centred on marginalised women and reproductive care leans toward guaranteed public health care.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Advocates stress pay inequality and low-paid women's work; Me Too commentary links harassment to tipped wages, so a higher minimum is a natural inference.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: The movement criticises corporate co-option and economic inequality, so it is unlikely to trust markets over governments, though it has no market theory.

public-ownership.rationale: Adherents rarely address ownership of utilities; the movement's economic concerns are pay, care and harassment rather than nationalisation.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Concern with economic inequality among women suggests support for redistribution, but this is inferred rather than campaigned on.

unions-good.rationale: Workplace harassment campaigns favour collective worker protection and reporting channels, so unions are probably welcomed; inferred.

property-fundamental.rationale: Property rights are not a theme; the movement's equality focus makes absolute property protection an unlikely priority.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Me Too demands, such as penalties for firms keeping repeat harassers and limits on forced NDAs and arbitration, are corporate regulation.

cut-welfare.rationale: Joanna Williams criticises the movement for relying on the state; adherents would reject welfare cuts that hit women and carers hardest.

worker-ownership.rationale: Worker ownership is not a fourth-wave theme and adherents range from liberal to socialist, so the movement is indifferent.

surveillance-ok.rationale: No stated position; concern for marginalised groups and distrust of policing in Me Too critiques suggests scepticism of mass surveillance.

legalize-drugs.rationale: The movement has no drug policy and its liberal and radical wings differ; adherents are split.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Online harassment of women is a central grievance, and adherents tend to favour limits on abuse, though free-speech concerns are not absent.

strong-leader.rationale: The movement's grassroots, hashtag-driven and anti-hierarchical form and its opposition to male dominance make a strong-leader solution alien.

state-harmful.rationale: Adherents press the state for laws on harassment, rape kits and equal pay, so they plainly regard the state as necessary.

limit-guns.rationale: Not addressed directly; gender-based violence concerns and a broadly progressive outlook suggest support for gun limits.

empower-police-military.rationale: Me Too critics fault the movement for ignoring police misconduct, and adherents distrust institutions that fail survivors; no direct position.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Adherents are genuinely split between sex-work-inclusive and abolitionist feminists; critics say Me Too excluded sex workers.

decide-locally.rationale: National and international legal change on harassment and abortion is the goal, so devolution is not a priority; inferred.

rehabilitation.rationale: Survivor-centred accountability sits alongside concern for incarcerated women; adherents are split between punitive and restorative approaches.

traditional-family.rationale: Adherents argue that gender roles push women into homemaking and promote gender-neutral child-rearing, rejecting the traditional family as society's foundation.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: The movement is described as more inclusive of LGBTQ+ people and queer feminism, so legal same-sex marriage is a settled commitment.

abortion-legal.rationale: Abortion rights mobilised mass protests after Dobbs and the Argentine green-scarf movement, showing it as a core cause.

more-religion-public.rationale: Not a stated topic, but reproductive and LGBTQ+ rights conflict with a larger public role for religion; inferred.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Intersectional commitment to women of colour and marginalised groups implies active redress of racial injustice.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Fourth-wave sources treat gender roles as imposed norms and promote gender-neutral upbringing, though not every adherent denies biology.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: No stated position; opposition to traditional gender norms makes cultural preservation for its own sake unattractive.

gradual-change.rationale: The movement uses fast viral campaigns to demand immediate change, though it also seeks institutional reform; leaning against gradualism.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Inclusive, intersectional outlook concerned with marginalised groups suggests opposition to cutting immigration; inferred.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Campaigns such as HeForShe and transnational hashtag movements engage UN-style bodies; inferred sympathy.

free-trade.rationale: Not addressed; the movement is critical of corporate power but has no trade doctrine.

nation-first.rationale: The movement is transnational, spreading through local hashtags in many countries, which contradicts a nation-first stance.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: No stated position on military intervention; adherents split between human-rights interventionism and anti-war views.

open-borders.rationale: Sympathetic to marginalised migrants but no movement position on open borders; adherents differ.

limit-growth.rationale: Not a fourth-wave theme; adherents vary between eco-feminist and mainstream growth views.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Not central, but the progressive base and intersectional framing support strong climate action; inferred.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: The movement uses digital tools for activism yet highlights online harassment and unequal tech access, so it is mixed.

expand-nuclear.rationale: No position on nuclear power; adherents unlikely to agree and the issue is not addressed.

revolution-justified.rationale: The movement works through hashtags, protest and law reform rather than revolution; inferred.

experts-over-public.rationale: Its stress on lived experience and survivor testimony over institutional authority suggests distrust of expert-only decisions.

central-planning.rationale: No stated view; the movement's concerns are not about planning and its liberal wing opposes it.

socialized-markets.rationale: Economic organisation is not addressed and adherents range from liberal to socialist.

land-value-tax.rationale: Entirely outside the movement's concerns; no inference possible.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Concern for economic inequality implies some sympathy for taxing inherited wealth; inferred.

basic-income.rationale: Recognising unpaid care labour and women's economic inequality makes a basic income attractive; inferred rather than documented.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Not addressed; no reason for a particular stance.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Industrial policy is outside the movement's concerns.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Distribution of property among small owners is not part of the movement's agenda, and the sources give no lead.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Adherents campaign for pay equity within the wage system, not for abolishing wages.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: No sympathy expected for market-anarchist monetary proposals; inferred from the pro-state, pro-regulation outlook.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: State-recognised employer and worker bodies setting wages are not discussed in fourth-wave sources; the movement's pay demands are about equal pay.

one-party-rule.rationale: The movement's decentralised, pluralist, voice-giving character is opposed to single-party guidance.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Hereditary privilege conflicts with the equality focus, though monarchy is not discussed; inferred.

democracy-best.rationale: Adherents seek change through public pressure, law and elections and value equal voice; the "even when voters choose badly" clause tempers it.

direct-votes.rationale: Not a movement position; adherents are unlikely to be consistent either way.

workers-councils.rationale: Not addressed; mainstream fourth-wave activism works within legislatures and courts.

right-to-secede.rationale: Regional secession is unrelated to the movement's campaigns on harassment and gender equality, so no position follows.

natural-rulers.rationale: The movement attacks male privilege and rigid hierarchies of sex, so claims that some are naturally fit to rule run directly against it.

political-violence-never.rationale: Campaigns are nonviolent hashtag and protest movements; adherents mostly reject violence though not absolutely.

war-builds-character.rationale: Critique of toxic masculinity makes the idea that war builds character unwelcome.

separate-church-state.rationale: Reproductive and LGBTQ+ rights give adherents reason to want religion out of lawmaking; inferred.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Scripture-based law conflicts directly with abortion rights, LGBTQ+ equality and gender-equality aims.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Adherents seek public legal remedies such as anti-harassment law, so privatised justice is rejected; inferred.

military-superiority.rationale: No direct position; the movement's concerns and its progressive base lean against military primacy.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Intersectional, inclusive framing rejects ethnically defined nations.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Intersectional theory sees class as one of several interlocking systems rather than the main driver, so adherents are split.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Pay-gap and equal-income demands favour equal outcomes, though adherents do not all frame it that way.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Intersectional concern for marginalised groups suggests support; inferred.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Not a core fourth-wave demand but consistent with intersectional anti-racism; inferred.

civilizational-union.rationale: Political union of nations sharing a civilization is not a fourth-wave topic and nothing in its principles points either way.

self-interest-moral.rationale: The movement stresses solidarity and collective action, so celebrating self-interest as moral is unlikely.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Rights claims by individuals and survivors are central; inferred.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: The sources on the movement do not discuss environmental philosophy, and adherents range from eco-feminists to those uninterested.

limit-population.rationale: Reproductive autonomy is central, so state-driven limits are opposed even though access to contraception is supported.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: No position; the movement is not anti-industrial.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Not addressed; digital activism is embraced but disruption as a goal is not.

human-enhancement.rationale: Bodily enhancement through technology is not a theme, though bodily autonomy might sway some adherents either way.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Not addressed; scepticism inferred from concern about unaccountable systems and marginalised groups.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Not addressed; privacy concerns for survivors versus safety concerns split adherents.

restore-past-order.rationale: The movement challenges inherited gender hierarchies and pushes for progress, so restoring a lost order is opposed.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Adherents are ideologically committed but pragmatic about campaigning; no stated stance.

direct-action.rationale: Hashtag and street protest are used alongside lobbying for laws and elections, so adherents use both.

means-match-ends.rationale: Survivor-centred, inclusive organising is meant to model the equality it seeks; inferred from Burke's empathy-based approach.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Entirely outside the movement; a rejection of modern life is not part of its aims.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Adherents criticise gendered divisions of labour, not division of labour as such.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Not addressed; adherents range from liberal to socialist.

production-for-use.rationale: Production for need rather than profit is a socialist idea that some adherents hold, but the movement as a whole does not take it up.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Some adherents critique capitalism but the movement has no unified labour theory; split.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Outside the movement's methods and incompatible with its pluralist, voice-giving politics.

collective-farming.rationale: Farming organisation is outside the movement's concerns and sources give nothing to infer from.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: No stated position; not a fourth-wave concern.

taxation-theft.rationale: Adherents seek state action and public funding and do not regard taxation as theft.

harm-principle.rationale: Adherents accept limits to prevent harm but also back restrictions beyond direct harm, such as on harassment and hate speech, so split.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Intersectionality attends to group-based oppression and structural inequality, so rights are not purely individual.

conscription.rationale: Not addressed; mostly opposed by progressive adherents, and gender-neutral draft views vary.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Movement is entirely about voice, collective speaking out, rather than exit.

state-as-business.rationale: Adherents see government as a provider of rights and protection, not a business; inferred.

positive-liberty.rationale: Concern with the material and social conditions for women's freedom suggests agreement; inferred.

media-academia-power.rationale: The movement treats media and elites as sites of sexism, not as dominant power, but does not address the claim directly.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Intersectional anti-racism treats racial differences as social, not genetic, so the claim is rejected.

organic-representation.rationale: Not addressed; adherents seek individual political voice for women through ordinary institutions.

total-state.rationale: A state directing all of life is incompatible with the movement's emphasis on personal autonomy and bodily choice.

national-rebirth.rationale: Not addressed; rhetoric of decadence and rebirth conflicts with the movement's progressive framing.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Not addressed; foreign expansion is contrary to the movement's progressive, transnational outlook.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Feudal loyalty rule is outside the movement and contradicts its equality aims.

bound-labor.rationale: Legally bound labour contradicts the movement's basic commitments to equality and freedom from coercion.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Adherents stress lived experience and challenge supposed neutrality, as in intersectional critiques of single-axis frameworks, though not as a doctrine.

universal-morality.rationale: Universal rights claims coexist with situated-knowledge views, so adherents are split.

single-common-good.rationale: Intersectionality stresses competing group interests and difference over one common good.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Not addressed; adherents are sharply divided on this question.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Diaspora return rights are not addressed by the movement; its concerns are gender-based violence and inequality.

revive-national-language.rationale: Language revival is not discussed by the fourth-wave sources, so no stance can be derived.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Worker voice on harassment and workplace policy suggests sympathy for democratic say over firms; inferred.

school-vouchers.rationale: Not addressed; progressive adherents favour public schooling and the sex-education curricula Burke backs.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: No stated position; progressive, pro-public-spending leaning suggests disagreement.

economic-freedom.rationale: Not addressed; adherents range from market liberals to socialists.

rule-by-example.rationale: Adherents demand laws and accountability for powerful men's conduct, not reliance on rulers' example.

national-self-determination.rationale: National self-determination is not a fourth-wave issue; adherents' views come from other political commitments and vary.

force-without-un.rationale: No stated position; progressive and internationalist leaning suggests scepticism.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Not addressed; adherents include religious and secular feminists, and value both testimony and evidence.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Concern for migrant and marginalised women suggests opposing citizen-only welfare; inferred.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Recognition of unpaid care labour makes work requirements for welfare unattractive; inferred.

class-collaboration.rationale: Not addressed; adherents split between liberal workplace reform and class-conflict views.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Futurist sacrifice of cultural institutions is unrelated to and contrary to the movement's aims.

dominated-front.rationale: A common front against Western powers is a geopolitical question the movement does not address and its adherents are mostly Western-based.

workers-nation.rationale: The movement is transnational and intersectional, not nationally organised; inferred.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: The movement exists to dismantle gendered roles; Wikipedia describes feminists arguing rigid gender roles harm both women and men.

ban-interest.rationale: Not addressed; no inclination toward religious finance rules.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Intersectionality was developed to expose and fight race-based discrimination, so racial segregation law is rejected outright.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Adherents see the state as both a patriarchal institution and a needed ally for reform, so they are split.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: No stated position; progressive leaning suggests opposition.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Inclusive, intersectional framing respects the cultures of marginalised groups; inferred.

elite-replacement.rationale: Conspiracy theories about elites replacing populations are rejected by the movement as racist and unsupported.

proportional-representation.rationale: Not a movement issue, but proportional systems tend to improve women's representation; inferred.

national-mission.rationale: Not addressed; a mission to spread a national model contradicts the movement's anti-hierarchical stance.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Systemic male advantage is the movement's core diagnosis, with male privilege, rape culture and everyday sexism as its recurring concepts.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Me Too and Everyday Sexism show powerful men protected by institutions, though this is not framed as general political corruption.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Eugenic restriction of reproduction contradicts the movement's defence of bodily and reproductive autonomy.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Accountability for abuse of power is a central theme of the movement; extending it to security forces is inferred.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Demands for harassment law, rape kit processing and school policy require a much more active state.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Intersectional anti-racism rejects any discouragement of interracial marriage.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Equal worth and equal rights regardless of sex and race is the movement's foundation.

socialism-one-country.rationale: This is an internal debate of Marxist-Leninist socialism that fourth-wave feminism does not engage.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Not addressed by the movement; adherents' views split.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Adherents split between uniform equal law and respect for minority religious communities; not addressed.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Not addressed; liberal freedom-of-belief leaning suggests opposition.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Not addressed; no inclination to religiously motivated bans.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Sex education and gender equality in schools are demands that favour secular state schooling; inferred.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Not addressed; a growing state runs against the movement's civil-liberty leanings.

consent-of-governed.rationale: The movement stresses voice and consent, particularly in sexual contexts, which carries over; political legitimacy itself is not discussed.

trade-surplus.rationale: Export-import balance is a mercantilist concern with no link to the movement's campaigns.

population-transfer.rationale: Forced removal of a minority contradicts the movement's inclusive, intersectional commitments.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Libertarian absolutism is not part of the movement and it supports state force against abusers, so it is not a doctrine here.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: The movement emphasises cooperation and solidarity and criticises competitive masculinity norms.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Not addressed; adherents split between protecting speech and banning hate groups.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Resistance to male power over women even when unexercised resembles this idea, but republican theory is not its language.

separated-powers.rationale: Constitutional design of checks and balances is not a topic in the sources; adherents use courts and legislatures without a stated theory.

vanguard-party.rationale: The movement is decentralised and online with no vanguard, and its critics say it lacks leadership.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Intersectional concern for the most marginalised implies giving priority to the poor; inferred.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Council housing sales are a UK housing-policy matter the movement has not taken a position on.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Workplace-rights concerns suggest opposition to restricting strikes; inferred.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Intersectional theory attributes poverty to structural inequality, not population.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Intersectional and inclusive framing treats diversity as a strength and rejects this claim.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Sortition for public office is not discussed; the movement seeks more women in elected office rather than lottery selection.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Strong emphasis on protection of rights suggests opposition; not directly discussed.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Price controls on staple foods are not mentioned in the sources and fall outside the movement's agenda.

party-controls-media.rationale: The movement relies on free online media to speak out and so opposes state control of media.

party-commands-army.rationale: Not addressed; opposed by the movement's democratic leaning.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Concern for migrant women suggests opposition; inferred.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Capping representatives' pay is not discussed by the movement or its sources.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Internal party discipline is not covered by a movement that organises through loose networks rather than parties.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Transnational outlook suggests mild support; inferred.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Not addressed; executive concentration conflicts with the movement's wariness of concentrated power.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Church governance is a matter for believers, and the sources show the movement taking no position on it.

clerical-rule.rationale: Rule by religious scholars is incompatible with the movement's reproductive and LGBTQ+ rights agenda.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Revolutionary defeatism in great-power war is a Marxist-Leninist doctrine that fourth-wave feminism does not take up.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Adherents criticise sexist media but mostly favour criticism, not state censorship; inferred.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Not addressed; concentration of power is distrusted.

recall-officials.rationale: Public accountability of those in power is a recurring theme; inferred.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Military alliances and overseas troop deployments are not discussed by the movement and no position follows from its principles.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Abolishing renting is not part of the agenda, and adherents are unlikely to support banning a common tenure form.

people-in-arms.rationale: Not addressed; gun-control leaning suggests opposition.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Not addressed; no inclination to romanticise rural life.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Reunification of divided nations is not covered by the movement and its sources.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Not addressed; movement draws heavily on educated activists and academics.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Respect for cultural difference sits uneasily with criticism of oppressive practices, so adherents split.

death-penalty.rationale: Not addressed directly; progressive leaning suggests opposition, though some advocate harsh punishment for sexual violence.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Burke calls for sex education that teaches children to report predators, and gender-equality education is a standard aim.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Not addressed; progressive and science-oriented outlook opposes it.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Feminists are split between anti-porn and sex-positive camps; fourth-wave sources show no settled position.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Not addressed; inclusive leaning suggests opposition.

minority-language-support.rationale: Inclusive treatment of marginalised groups suggests support; inferred.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Adherents split between freedom of religion and enforcing equality law.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Opposition to conformist gender norms suggests agreement with encouraging nonconformist lives.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Third-world debt policy is not discussed in the sources; some adherents of the intersectional left support cancellation, but not as a movement position.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Decolonial economic transformation is not a fourth-wave subject, so the movement has no stated view.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Not addressed; recent feminist-backed constitutional processes exist but no position is documented.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Not addressed; strongly contrary to rights-centred outlook.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Intersectional and transnational outlook suggests support; inferred.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Nuclear deterrence policy is not addressed by the sources or the movement's campaigns.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: The method of choosing a head of state is not a topic in fourth-wave sources.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Central bank independence is a technical economic question the movement does not address.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Territorial concessions in peace deals are not discussed by the movement and adherents are divided on the underlying conflicts.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Egalitarian outlook sits with limiting property rights for social ends; inferred.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: The nature of the Soviet economy is a debate within Marxism and is not engaged by fourth-wave feminism.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Not addressed; progressive leaning suggests support.

collective-defense.rationale: Mutual-defence treaties are not discussed by the movement, so no position can be derived.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: The legal status of annexed territory is outside the movement's concerns and sources.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Not addressed; adherents split on how far to curb religious institutions.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: A symbolic non-party head of state is not a topic in the movement.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Not addressed; force against a region's wishes conflicts with consent-based politics.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Arrangements such as one country, two systems are not discussed by the fourth-wave sources.

sacred-ruler.rationale: A sacred ruler contradicts the movement's equality and anti-hierarchy values.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Concern for economic inequality favours progressive taxation; inferred.

character-from-environment.rationale: Sources describe the movement attributing gender differences to social norms and upbringing, though not denying all innate traits.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Me Too targets powerful men escaping accountability, so rulers above the law are rejected.

space-expansion.rationale: Space expansion is not a goal or concern of the movement and adherents show no consistent view.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Classical mixed-constitution theory is not part of fourth-wave discourse.

leader-cult.rationale: Hero-worship of leaders conflicts with the movement's grassroots, anti-hierarchy character and its critique of powerful men.

equal-parenting.rationale: Adherents back shared parenting but also worry about abusive partners; split on a legal presumption.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: This is a Maoist doctrine that fourth-wave feminism does not discuss.

land-redistribution.rationale: Land reform is not a theme in the sources on the movement, which concentrates on gender-based harms.

refugee-return.rationale: Concern for displaced and marginalised people suggests support; inferred.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Territorial claims on ethnic grounds contradict the movement's inclusive stance.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Punishing apostasy conflicts with the movement's rights-based, anti-coercive commitments.

women-must-cover.rationale: Legally compelled dress for women conflicts with bodily autonomy, central to the movement, and with opposition to body policing.

common-currency.rationale: Currency union is an economic question not addressed by the movement.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Ethnic unity projects are not part of the movement; inclusive outlook suggests mild disagreement.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Minority cultural self-government is not discussed in the sources; the movement's aim is inclusion within existing institutions.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: The movement's emphasis on fighting for equal rights within existing societies resembles this stance; inferred.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Intersectionality stresses interlocking systems and representation, not material production alone; adherents split.

no-bailouts.rationale: Bank and firm bailouts are not covered by the sources; adherents' economic views vary too much to infer a position.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: The movement relies on courts and rights to protect minorities from majorities; inferred.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Equal representation of women is a standard feminist demand and is in line with the movement's equality aims.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Autarky is not addressed and conflicts with the movement's transnational character.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Concern for workers and equity suggests support; inferred.

moral-incentives.rationale: Replacing material with moral incentives is a Guevarist idea absent from fourth-wave discourse.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: The movement's nonviolent organising rejects this.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Opposition to privilege generally suggests support; hereditary titles are not discussed.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Inclusive and intersectional education aims suggest opposition to nation-centred history.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Intersectional anti-racism rejects rule of "less advanced" societies by "more advanced" ones.

patriotic-education.rationale: Not addressed; mild opposition inferred from the movement's critical and inclusive stance.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Intersectional concern for women of colour suggests defending preferences, but this is not directly stated.

public-money-creation.rationale: Monetary-system reform is not discussed by the movement or its sources.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Capitalism's long-run crisis tendencies are not a fourth-wave subject; some adherents critique it, others accept it.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Anti-colonial leaning in intersectional thought suggests opposition; inferred.

delink-world-market.rationale: Dependency-theory delinking is not addressed by the movement.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: The labour aristocracy thesis is a Marxist debate the movement has not engaged.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Intersectionality arose from discrimination law, and the movement opposes discrimination by employers and services.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Rights protection is favoured; entrenchment is inferred.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: The validity of colonial-era borders is not discussed in the sources on the movement.

elective-rulers.rationale: Elective government is consistent with the movement's democratic leaning; not discussed.

minority-veto.rationale: Not addressed; individual vetoes would block reform, and the movement seeks change through majority action.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Me Too holds powerful figures to account, so resisting lawless rulers is consistent; no direct statement.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Not addressed; adherents rely on both legislatures and courts.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Not a theme; progressive base generally agrees that animals' suffering matters.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Not addressed; adherents range from vegans to omnivores.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: The movement demands structural change, not charity from privileged people, though privilege awareness is a theme.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: The movement is explicitly about public speaking out and political participation, so withdrawal is rejected.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Intersectional representation critique treats media as reproducing stereotypes and harm, though adherents do not use the pacification framing.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Not addressed in these terms; adherents' view of hegemony varies.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: World-systems theory is not part of the movement's discourse, though some intersectional thinkers draw on it.

native-born-offices.rationale: Reserving offices for the native-born is not discussed, but it conflicts with inclusive aims and is opposed on that inference.

party-own-road.rationale: Relations among communist parties are not an issue for the movement.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Development strategy for poor countries is not addressed in the sources on the movement.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Irredentist demands are not addressed by the sources, and adherents have no common line.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Support for indigenous rights is plausible but political primacy over settlers is not addressed.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Progressive anti-authoritarian leaning suggests agreement; not stated.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Comparison of fascism and communism is a historiographical dispute the movement does not engage.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Intersectional anti-racism and historical consensus identify slavery as the main cause.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Not addressed; anti-racist and anti-sexist leaning suggests supporting removal, but this is inferred.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Sources note rigid masculinity harms men and the movement invites men in, but adherents are wary of equating male and female disadvantage.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Movement treats gender-based violence as primarily violence against women within structural inequality, rejecting equal-seriousness symmetry claims.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Universal rights language in gender equality campaigns opposes civilizational relativism; inferred.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Not addressed; military political role conflicts with the movement's civilian democratic orientation.

paid-care-work.rationale: The movement criticises pressure toward homemaking and unequal economic burdens on women, so paid recognition of care work is a natural claim.

filial-duty.rationale: Adult children's duties to parents are not covered by the sources; adherents are split between obligation to family and critique of patriarchal family duties.

office-by-exam.rationale: Civil service recruitment is not addressed by the movement.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Screening foreign investment is an economic-policy matter not covered by the movement.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Adherents hold that women should leave marriages freely, and gender-role critique rejects forced marriage bonds.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Imperative mandates for representatives are not a topic in fourth-wave discourse.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Not addressed; gaps in women's lifetime earnings make private-account pensions unattractive; inferred.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Use-based land tenure is not discussed in the sources on the movement.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Parliamentary budget control is not a fourth-wave issue, and the movement has no stated constitutional theory.

single-official-language.rationale: Inclusive outlook suggests mild opposition; inferred.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Not addressed; inclusive outlook suggests mild opposition.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Crenshaw's DeGraffenreid argument is that courts overlooked compound discrimination despite unequal outcomes, so adherents favour impact-based discrimination tests.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Body-image critiques of advertising suggest a negative view of status-driven consumerism, though not a stated doctrine.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Covert support for foreign insurgents is not addressed; a mild lean against it is inferred from the movement's nonviolent character.

corporate-influence.rationale: Critique of corporate co-option and of firms shielding harassers supports agreement; not stated explicitly.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Feminist NGOs often depend on international funding; inferred.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Reproductive-autonomy focus makes state pressure to have children unwelcome.

residents-only-property.rationale: Not addressed; inclusive outlook suggests mild opposition.

job-guarantee.rationale: Concern with women's economic inequality suggests sympathy; inferred.

democratic-peace.rationale: Democratic peace theory is an international-relations claim the movement does not address.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Adherents split between defying unjust law and relying on law for protection.

non-intervention.rationale: Transnational solidarity and human-rights framing suggest rejection of absolute non-intervention; inferred.

industrial-unions.rationale: Union structure by industry or craft is not discussed by the movement.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Conspiracy theories against ethnic or religious minorities are contrary to intersectional anti-discrimination.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Adherents split between abolition and reforming marriage equality; not a movement position.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Transparency about abuse is in line with the movement's documentation approach; not stated.

local-production.rationale: Localism in production is not part of fourth-wave concerns, which centre on gender and discrimination.

informal-organisation.rationale: Hashtag-based, leaderless organising matches this style, though adherents also use formal groups.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Transnational outlook suggests mild opposition; inferred.

religious-nation.rationale: Defining the nation by religion excludes minorities and conflicts with inclusive aims.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Not addressed; mild opposition inferred from anti-hierarchy.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Regional fiscal arrangements are not addressed by the movement's sources.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: The distinction between personal and productive property is not discussed in the sources on the movement.

defeat-communism.rationale: The movement has no Cold War stance; a mild disagreement is inferred from its non-confrontational, progressive leaning.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Provider mix in public services is a technical policy question the movement has not addressed.

religion-illusion.rationale: Religion as illusion is not a feminist claim here; adherents include religious feminists.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Mixed: Wikipedia reports corporate campaigns as inimical to the movement but liberal adherents accept markets.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Sources stress economic inequalities, equal pay and critique of capitalism's corporate co-option, though not all adherents call for system change.

socialized-care.rationale: Support for public childcare is plausible but sources show adherents divided on socialising care entirely; not addressed.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Linguistic purism is not a fourth-wave topic; a slight disagreement is inferred from its inclusive outlook.

treaties-binding.rationale: Treaties with internal nations are not discussed in the sources; supporters of indigenous rights might agree but it is not stated.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Self-governing cooperative communities are an anarchist or utopian idea outside the mainstream movement.

majority-settlement.rationale: Settling majorities into minority regions conflicts with minority protection.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: A third way between capitalism and communism is not argued by fourth-wave sources, and adherents' economic views are mixed.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Historical or religious land claims are not addressed by the movement; adherents are divided by their other commitments.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Denial is a falsehood that adherents reject as racist hate, consistent with intersectional anti-discrimination.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: The movement is described as inclusive of LGBTQ+ people and queer feminism.

suppress-opposition.rationale: The movement is about expanding voice, so suppressing opposition is rejected.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Punishing blasphemy contradicts the movement's rights framework.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: This Islamist doctrine is not addressed in the sources, and the movement has no position on it.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Violent removal of rulers for not following religious law contradicts the movement's nonviolent, rights-based politics.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Giving marginalised women direct voice through participatory networks is central, as the movement's online organising shows.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Intersectionality, from Crenshaw, is described as central to the movement and holds that race, gender and class overlap.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: The movement is described as generally inclusive of trans people, though a trans-exclusionary faction exists, so a typical adherent agrees at +1.

assisted-dying.rationale: Assisted dying is not a fourth-wave issue and adherents divide between autonomy and disability-rights concerns.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: The movement sits on the political left and does not see left-right as obsolete; inferred.

alienated-labor.rationale: Marx's alienation thesis is not taken up by the movement, though socialist adherents might accept it.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Intersectional anti-racism rejects such claims as prejudice.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Not addressed; armed intervention to hold a state in a bloc contradicts the movement's consent-based, anti-domination politics.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Milano and others call for banning mandatory NDAs and arbitration clauses in employment as a central Me Too legal demand.

missingStatements.text: Employers should not be able to use nondisclosure agreements or mandatory arbitration to keep sexual harassment complaints out of court.
missingStatements.rationale: Milano and others call for banning mandatory NDAs and arbitration clauses in employment as a central Me Too legal demand.

missingStatements.text: Men and boys should be actively engaged as partners in achieving gender equality.
missingStatements.rationale: HeForShe invites men to support equality and Burke says the movement is for everyone, including men.
missingStatements.declined: Near-universally agreed, so it would not discriminate between ideologies; male-disadvantage-attention covers the contested part.

notes: Adherents are divided on sex work and pornography, and on trans inclusion (a trans-exclusionary faction exists). Economic positions are inferred and vary from liberal to anti-capitalist.
